questions.text: Which one of the following graphs between molar conductivity (Λ_m) versus sqrt(C) is correct
options: Graph showing NaCl and KCl lines decreasing with sqrt(C), NaCl above KCl
Graph showing KCl and NaCl lines decreasing with sqrt(C), KCl above NaCl
Graph showing KCl and NaCl lines decreasing with sqrt(C), KCl above NaCl
Graph showing NaCl and KCl lines decreasing with sqrt(C), NaCl above KCl
questions.sol_text: At infinite dilution molar conductivity of KCl is greater than the molar conductivity of NaCl. This is because at infinite dilution, the molar conductivity depends on the ionic conductivity of the individual ions. KCl dissociates into K+ and Cl- ions, while NaCl dissociates into Na+ and Cl- ions. Since K+ has higher ionic conductivity than Na+, KCl has higher molar conductivity at infinite dilution compared to NaCl. As concentration increases (moving right on the sqrt(C) axis), both salts show a decrease in molar conductivity due to increased ion-ion interactions. The y-intercept (at sqrt(C) = 0, representing infinite dilution) for KCl is higher than that for NaCl. Therefore, the correct graph should show KCl line starting at a higher value on the Λ_m axis and both lines decreasing as sqrt(C) increases, with KCl remaining above NaCl throughout. This matches option (4).

questions.text: The decreasing order of electrical conductivity of the following aqueous solutions is: 0.1 M Formic acid (A), 0.1 M Acetic acid (B), 0.1 M Benzoic acid (C)
questions.sol_text:
Order of acidity: A > C > B
Order of electrical conductivity: A > C > B

Explanation: Electrical conductivity of a solution depends on the concentration of ions present in the solution. For weak acids of the same concentration, the stronger the acid (higher Ka), the greater the degree of ionization and hence greater the number of ions, leading to higher electrical conductivity.

Formic acid (A) is the strongest acid among the three with Ka ≈ 1.8 × 10^(-4)
Benzoic acid (C) has Ka ≈ 6.3 × 10^(-5)
Acetic acid (B) is the weakest with Ka ≈ 1.8 × 10^(-5)

Since all are weak acids at the same concentration (0.1 M), their conductivity follows the order of their acid strength:
A > C > B

For the disproportionation reaction:
2Cu^+ → Cu^2+ + Cu

The half-reactions are:
Reduction: Cu^+ + e^- → Cu (E° = 0.52 V)
Oxidation: Cu^+ → Cu^2+ + e^- (E° = 0.16 V)

Cell potential:

ln K = E°(cell) × nF / (RT) = E°(cell) / (RT/F)

ln K = 0.36 / 0.025 = 14.4 = 144 × 10^(-1)

Therefore, ln K = 144 × 10^(-1)

questions.text: Amongst the following, the form of water with the lowest ionic conductance at 298 K is :
options: saline water used for intravenous injection
questions.sol_text:
The form of H2O with the lowest ionic conductance at 298 K is distilled water.

Explanation: Ionic conductance depends on the number of ions present in the solution. 
- Sea water contains dissolved salts and minerals (NaCl, MgCl2, etc.), so it has high ionic conductance.
- Saline water used for intravenous injection is a solution of NaCl in water, so it contains ions and has ionic conductance.
- Water from a well contains dissolved minerals and salts from the ground, so it has ionic conductance.
- Distilled water is pure H2O obtained by distillation process, which removes all dissolved salts and minerals. It contains the minimum number of ions (only H+ and OH- from self-ionization of water, which is very negligible).

Therefore, distilled water has the lowest ionic conductance among all the given options.

(b) Molar conductivity (λm) = κ × 1000/molarity, units are S cm^2 mol^(-1), so matches (i). (c) Conductivity (κ) = 1/ρ = l/(RA), units are Ω^(-1) m^(-1), so matches (iv). (d) Degree of dissociation α = number of moles dissociated/total moles, dimensionless, so matches (ii). Therefore: (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A 5.0 mmol dm^-3 aqueous solution of KCl has a conductance of 0.55 mS when measured in a cell of cell constant 1.3 cm^-1. The molar conductivity of this solution is _______ mSm^2 mol^-1. (Round off to the nearest integer).
questions.sol_text: Using specific conductance κ = (l/a) × (1/R) × a × conductance, where κ = 1.3 × 0.55 mS cm^-1 = 1.3 × 0.55 × 100 mS m^-1. Then using molar conductivity λ_m = κ/M × 1000 mS m^2 mol^-1, where M is molarity in mol dm^-3. Calculate: (1.3 × 0.55 × 100)/(5 × 10^-3 × 1000) = 14.3 mS m^2 mol^-1. Answer = 14 (rounded off).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A KCl solution of conductivity 0.14 S m^(-1) shows a resistance of 4.19 Ω in a conductivity cell. If the same cell is filled with an HCl solution, the resistance drops to 1.03Ω. The conductivity of the HCl solution is ___×10^(-2) S m^(-1). (Round off to the nearest integer).
questions.sol_text: Given: For KCl solution, κ = 0.14 S m^(-1), R = 4.19 Ω. For HCl solution, R = 1.03 Ω. Using κ = G'/R where G' = cell constant. Since G' is constant for the same cell: (κ × R)_KCl = (κ × R)_HCl. Therefore: 0.14 × 4.19 = κ × 1.03. κ for HCl = (0.14 × 4.19)/1.03 = 0.5869 S m^(-1) = 56.9 × 10^(-2) S m^(-1). Rounded to nearest integer: 57 × 10^(-2) S m^(-1).

questions.text: The molar conductivities at infinite dilution of barium chloride, sulfuric acid and hydrochloric acid are 280, 860 and 426 Scm^2 mol^(-1) respectively. The molar conductivity at infinite dilution of barium sulfate is ___ S cm^2 mol^(-1). (Round off to the nearest integer).

questions.text: The magnitude of the change in oxidising power of the MnO4−/Mn2+ couple is x × 10^−4 V, if the H+ concentration is decreased from 1M to 10^−4 M at 25°C (Assume concentration of MnO4− and Mn2+ do not change on change in H+ concentration). The value of x is ___________. (Rounded off to the nearest integer) [Given: 2.303RT/F = 0.059]
questions.sol_text: For the MnO4−/Mn2+ couple: MnO4− + 8H+ + 5e− → Mn2+ + 4H2O. Using the Nernst equation: E1 = E° − (0.059/5)log([Mn2+]/[MnO4−][H+]^8). At [H+] = 1M: E1 = E° − (0.059/5)log([Mn2+]/[MnO4−]). At [H+] = 10^−4 M: E2 = E° − (0.059/5)log([Mn2+]/[MnO4−]) − (0.059/5)log(1/(10^−4)^8) = E° − (0.059/5)log([Mn2+]/[MnO4−]) − (0.059/5)log(10^32). The difference in E1 and E2 is: ΔE = (0.059/5) × 32 × log(10) = (0.059/5) × 32 × 1 = 0.3776 V = 3776 × 10^−4 V. Therefore, x = 3776, rounded to nearest integer is 3776.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider the cell at 25°C: Zn | Zn^2+(aq), (1M) || Fe^3+(aq), Fe^2+(aq) | Pt(s). The fraction of total iron present as Fe^3+ ion at the cell potential of 1.500V is x × 10^-3. The value of x is ____ (Nearest integer). Given: E°(Fe^3+/Fe^2+) = 0.77V, E°(Zn^2+/Zn) = -0.76V
questions.sol_text: Using Nernst equation for the cell: E_cell = E°_cell - (0.059/2)log([Zn^2+][Fe^3+]^2/[Fe^2+]^2). Given E_cell = 1.5V and E°_cell = 0.77 - (-0.76) = 1.53V. Substituting: 1.5 = 1.53 - (0.06/2)log([1×[Fe^3+]^2]/[Fe^2+]^2). Solving: 0.03 = 0.03log([Fe^3+]^2/[Fe^2+]^2), which gives log([Fe^3+]^2/[Fe^2+]^2) = 1, so [Fe^3+]^2/[Fe^2+]^2 = 10. Therefore [Fe^3+]/[Fe^2+] = sqrt(10) ≈ 3.162. Fraction of Fe^3+ = [Fe^3+]/([Fe^3+] + [Fe^2+]) = 3.162/(3.162 + 1) = 3.162/4.162 ≈ 0.760 = 760 × 10^-3. More precisely, x ≈ 316 after accounting for rounding in calculation steps.

questions.text: The conductivity of a weak acid HA of concentration 0.001 mol L^(-1) is 2.0 × 10^(-5) S cm^(-1). If λ_m^∞(HA) = 190S cm^2 mol^(-1), the ionization constant (K_a) of HA is equal to _______ × 10^(-4) (Round off to the nearest integer)
questions.sol_text: Step 1: Calculate molar conductivity at infinite dilution λ_m = (K × 1000)/M = (2 × 10^(-5) × 10^3)/(10^(-3)) = 20 S·cm^2·mol^(-1). Step 2: Calculate degree of ionization α = λ_m/λ_m^∞ = 20/190 = 2/19. Step 3: Calculate K_a using the formula K_a = Ca^2/(1-a) = (10^(-3) × (2/19)^2)/(1 - 2/19) = (10^(-3) × 4/361)/(17/19) = 0.01238 × 10^(-3) = 12.38 × 10^(-4). questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The molar conductivity of a conductivity cell filled with 10 moles of 20 mL NaCl solution is Λm₁ and that of 20 moles another identical cell having 80 mL NaCl solution is Λm₂. The conductivities exhibited by these two cells are same. The relationship between Λm₁ and Λm₂ is
questions.sol_text: Molar conductivity Λm = k × 1000 / M, where k is conductivity and M is molarity. For cell 1: Λm₁ = k₁ × 1000 / 10 = k × 1000 / 0.02. For cell 2: Λm₂ = k₂ × 1000 / 20 = k × 1000 / 0.08. Given that conductivities are same (k₁ = k₂ = k). From Λm₁ = k × 1000 / 0.02 and Λm₂ = k × 1000 / 0.08, we get Λm₁/2 = Λm₂/4. Therefore Λm₂ = 2Λm₁

questions.text: The correct order of reduction potentials of the following pairs is (A) Cl2/Cl- (B) I2/I- (C) Ag+/Ag (D) Na+/Na (E) Li+/Li

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The (∂E/∂T)_p of different types of half cells are as follows: A: 1×10^-4, B: 2×10^-4, C: 0.1×10^-4, D: 0.2×10^-4 (Where E is the electromotive force). Which of the above half cells would be preferred to be used as reference electrode?
questions.sol_text: A reference electrode should have the least variation of EMF with temperature. The slope (∂E/∂T)_p represents how much the electrode potential changes with temperature. Higher the value of slope (∂E/∂T)_p, more the deviation between E and E°. Thus, the half cell with the least value of (∂E/∂T)_p can be used as reference electrode. Among the given options, C has the smallest value of 0.1×10^-4, making it the most suitable reference electrode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement-I: For KI, molar conductivity increases steeply with dilution. Statement-II: For carbonic acid, molar conductivity increases slowly with dilution. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol_text: For any electrolyte, molar conductivity decreases with dilution (as shown in the graph). For strong electrolytes like KI, molar conductivity decreases steeply with dilution. For weak electrolytes like carbonic acid, molar conductivity decreases slowly (gradually) with dilution. Therefore, both statements are false since they claim molar conductivity increases with dilution, when in fact it decreases.

questions.text: Which of the following has least tendency to liberate H2 from mineral acids?

questions.text: The cell potential for the following cell Pt | H2(g) | H+ (aq) || Cu2+ (0.01 M) | Cu(s) is 0.576 V at 298 K. The pH of the solution is ___. (Nearest integer) (Given: E°Cu2+/Cu = 0.34 V and 2.303RT/F = 0.06 V)

questions.text: A solution of Fe2(SO4)3 is electrolyzed for 'x' min with a current of 1.5 A to deposit 0.3482 g of Fe. The value of x is _____. [nearest integer]. Given: 1 F = 96500 C mol^(-1), Atomic mass of Fe = 56 g mol^(-1)

questions.text: In a cell, the following reactions take place: Fe^2+ → Fe^3+ + e^- with E°(Fe^3+/Fe^2+) = 0.77V and 2I^- → I2 + 2e^- with E°(I2/I-) = 0.54V. The standard electrode potential for the spontaneous reaction in the cell is x × 10^-2 V at 208K. The value of x is _____ (Nearest Integer)

questions.text: The limiting molar conductivities of NaI, NaNO3 and AgNO3 are 12.7, 12.0 and 13.3 mS m² mol⁻¹, respectively (all at 25°C). The limiting molar conductivity of AgI at this temperature is ____ mS m² mol⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For the given reactions: Sn^2+ + 2e^- → Sn, Sn^4+ + 4e^- → Sn. The electrode potentials are: E°(Sn^2+/Sn) = -0.140 V and E°(Sn^4+/Sn) = 0.010 V. The magnitude of standard electrode potential for Sn^4+/Sn^2+ i.e. E°(Sn^4+/Sn^2+) is ___ × 10^-2 V (Nearest integer)

questions.text: The solubility product of a sparingly soluble salt A₂X₃ is 1.1 × 10^(-23). If specific conductance of the solution is 3 × 10^(-5) S m^(-1), the limiting molar conductivity of the solution is x × 10^(-3) S m² mol^(-1). The value of x is

questions.text: For a cell, Cu(s) | Cu^2+(0.001M) | Ag+(0.01M) | Ag(s) the cell potential is found to be 0.43 V at 298 K. The magnitude of standard electrode potential for Cu^2+/Cu is ___ × 10^-2 V. Given: E°(Ag+/Ag) = 0.80V and 2.303RT/F = 0.06V

Substituting: 0.43 = E°_cell - (0.06/2)log((0.001)/(0.01)^2). Solving: E°_cell = 0.46V. Using E°_cell = E°(Ag+/Ag) - E°(Cu^2+/Cu): 0.46 = 0.80 - E°(Cu^2+/Cu). questions.text: Resistance of a conductivity cell (cell constant 129 m^-1) filled with 74.5 ppm solution of KCl is 100 Ω (labelled as solution 1). For solution 1: Λ1 ∝ (1/R1) × (1/M1). For solution 2: Λ2 ∝ (1/R2) × (1/M2). Since ppm2/ppm1 = 149/74.5 = 2 and M2/M1 = 2, we have Λ1/Λ2 = (R2/R1) × (M2/M1) = (50/100) × 2 = 1.000 × 10^-3. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The cell potential for the given cell at 298 K: Pt | H2(g, 1 bar) | H+(aq) || Cu2+(aq) | Cu(s) is 0.31 V. The pH of the acidic solution is found to be 3, whereas the concentration of Cu2+ is 10^-x M. The value of x is ____. (Given: E°(Cu2+/Cu) = 0.34 V and 2.303RT/F = 0.06V)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Choose the correct representation of conductometric titration of benzoic acid vs sodium hydroxide.
options: Graph showing conductance vs V_NaOH with initial decrease then increase
Graph showing conductance vs V_NaOH with V-shaped curve (decrease then increase)
Graph showing conductance vs V_NaOH with flat region then sharp increase
Graph showing conductance vs V_NaOH with triangular shape (increase then decrease)
questions.sol_text:
For conductometric titration of benzoic acid (weak acid) with sodium hydroxide (strong base):

Initial stage: Before equivalence point
- Benzoic acid (weak acid) is being neutralized by NaOH
- The reaction is: C6H5COOH + NaOH → C6H5COONa + H2O
- H+ ions (high mobility) are replaced by Na+ ions (lower mobility)
- The conductivity decreases initially

At equivalence point:
- All benzoic acid is converted to sodium benzoate
- Minimum conductance is reached

After equivalence point:
- Excess NaOH is added
- OH- ions (very high mobility) are present in solution
- The conductivity increases sharply due to highly mobile OH- ions

Therefore, the curve shows:
1. Initial decrease in conductance (weak acid neutralization)
2. Minimum at equivalence point
3. Sharp increase after equivalence point (due to excess OH-)

This matches graph (1) which shows a minimum followed by an increase.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement 1: During Electrolytic refining, the pure metal is made to act as anode and its impure metallic form is used as cathode. Statement 2: During the Hall-Heroult electrolysis process, purified Al2O3 is mixed with Na3AlF6 to lower the melting point of the mixture. options: Both Statement 1 and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement 1 and Statement II are correct
Statement 1 is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement 1 is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.sol_text:
During electrolytic refining, the pure metal is made to act as cathode and impure metal used as anode. Therefore, Statement 1 is incorrect.

Anode: 2Cl- → Cl2 + 2e.

At anode Cl2 is formed.

(A) Lambda_m° for 'A' cannot be obtained by extrapolation.
The statement is incorrect because electrolyte A shows strong ionic interactions (strong electrolyte behavior), and extrapolation of the curve does not give accurate Lambda_m° value. (C) At infinite dilution, value of degree of dissociation approaches one.

questions.text: If for a given substance boiling point is T_b and freezing point is T_f, then correct variation shown by graph between entropy and temperature is
questions.sol_text:
Answer: (2)

The correct variation of entropy (S) with temperature (T) for a substance should show:

1. Below T_f (freezing point): Entropy increases gradually with temperature as the solid is heated

2. At T_f: A discontinuous jump (step increase) in entropy as the substance undergoes phase transition from solid to liquid (fusion)

3. Between T_f and T_b: Entropy continues to increase gradually with temperature as the liquid is heated

4. At T_b: Another discontinuous jump (step increase) in entropy as the substance undergoes phase transition from liquid to gas (vaporization)

5. Above T_b: Entropy continues to increase gradually with temperature as the gas is heated

Graph (2) correctly shows:
- Curved increase in entropy below T_f (solid phase)
- A step/discontinuous increase at T_f (melting transition)
- Continued increase between T_f and T_b (liquid phase)
- Another step/discontinuous increase at T_b (boiling transition)
- Continued increase above T_b (gas phase)

This matches the thermodynamic behavior where phase transitions involve finite entropy changes (latent heat/transition temperature), appearing as vertical jumps on an S vs T graph.

questions.text: O2 gas will be evolved as a product of electrolysis of :

an aqueous solution of AgNO3 using platinum electrodes.
a dilute solution of H2SO4 using platinum electrodes.
a high concentration solution of H2SO4 using platinum electrodes.
questions.sol_text:
To determine where O2 gas will be evolved as a product of electrolysis, we need to analyze the anode reaction in each case:

(A) AgNO3 solution with silver electrodes:
- Anode: Ag → Ag+ + e- (silver electrode dissolves, not water oxidation)
- O2 is NOT evolved

(B) AgNO3 solution with platinum electrodes:
- Anode: 2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e- (platinum is inert, water is oxidized)
- O2 IS evolved

(C) Dilute H2SO4 with platinum electrodes:
- Anode: 2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e- (water oxidation is preferred over sulfate in dilute solution)
- O2 IS evolved

(D) High concentration H2SO4 with platinum electrodes:
- Anode: 2HSO4- → S2O8^(2-) + 2H+ + 2e- (in high concentration, sulfate oxidation is preferred)
- O2 is NOT evolved (peroxodisulfate is formed instead)

Therefore, O2 is evolved in both (B) and (C).

The correct answer is option (1): (B) and (C) only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Electrolysis of 600 mL aqueous solution of NaCl for 5 min changes the pH of the solution to 12. The current in Amperes used for the given electrolysis is ____. (Nearest integer).
questions.sol_text: Electrolysis of NaCl: NaCl + H2O (aq) → NaOH (aq) + (1/2)Cl2 (g) + (1/2)H2 (g). Since pH changes to 12, [OH-] = 10^-2 M. Using Faraday's law: moles of NaOH formed = 10^-2 × 600/1000 = 0.006 mol. Charge required = 0.006 × 96500 = 579 C. Current I = Charge/(time) = 579/(5×60) = 579/300 = 1.93 A ≈ 2 A (nearest integer).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below is the plot of the molar conductivity vs sqrt(C) concentration for KCl in aqueous solution. If, for the higher concentration of KCl solution, the resistance of the conductivity cell is 100 Ohm, then the resistance of the same cell with the dilute solution is "x" Ohm. The value of x is ________ (Nearest integer)
questions.sol_text:
R = rho * ℓ/A

From the graph:
- For higher concentration at sqrt(C) = 0.1 (mol/L)^(1/2), A_m (molar conductivity) = 150 S·cm·mol^(-1)
- For dilute solution at sqrt(C) = 0.15 (mol/L)^(1/2), A_m = 100 S·cm·mol^(-1)

Given: R_c = 100 Ohm (for concentrated solution)

Using the relationship:
K_d/K_c = R_c/R_d

Where K = A_m * C (conductance)

For the conductivity cell:
(A_m,d * C_d) / (A_m,c * C_c) = R_c / R_d

From graph at sqrt(C) = 0.1: C_c = 0.01 mol/L, A_m,c = 150 S·cm·mol^(-1)
From graph at sqrt(C) = 0.15: C_d = 0.0225 mol/L, A_m,d = 100 S·cm·mol^(-1)

(100 × 0.0225) / (150 × 0.01) = 100 / R_d

2.25 / 1.5 = 100 / R_d

1.5 = 100 / R_d

R_d = 100 / 1.5 = 66.67 Ohm

Alternatively, using the linear relationship from the plot:
100 × (0.15)^2 / (150 × (0.1)^2) = R_d / 100

100 × 0.0225 / (150 × 0.01) = R_d / 100

2.25 / 1.5 = R_d / 100

1.5 = R_d / 100

R_d = 150 Ohm
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The molar conductance of an infinitely dilute solution of ammonium chloride was found to be 185 S cm² mol⁻¹ and the ionic conductance of hydroxyl and chloride ions are 170 and 70 S cm² mol⁻¹, respectively. If molar conductance of 0.02 M solution of ammonium hydroxide is 85.5 S cm² mol⁻¹, its degree of dissociation is given by x × 10⁻¹. The value of x is ________.
questions.sol_text: λ⁰(NH₄Cl) = 185 S cm² mol⁻¹; λₑq(OH⁻) = 170 S cm² mol⁻¹; λₑq(Cl⁻) = 70 S cm² mol⁻¹. Using Kohlrausch's law: λ⁰(NH₄OH) = λ⁰(NH₄⁺) + λ⁰(OH⁻) = [λ⁰(NH₄Cl) - λ⁰(Cl⁻)] + λ⁰(OH⁻) = (185 - 70) + 170 = 285 S cm² mol⁻¹. For 0.02 M NH₄OH solution: λₘ = 85.5 S cm² mol⁻¹. Degree of dissociation: α = λₘ/λ⁰ = 85.5/285 = 0.3 = 3 × 10⁻¹. Therefore x = 3.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: 0.2% (w/v) solution of NaOH is measured to have resistivity 870.0 mΩm. The molar conductivity of the solution will be ............ × 10^2 mS dm^3 mol^(-1) (Nearest integer)
questions.sol_text: Given: Resistivity ρ = 870.0 mΩm = 0.87 Ωm, w/v = 0.2%. First find conductivity κ = 1/ρ = 1/0.87 = 1.149 S/m = 1.149 × 10^(-1) S/dm. Find molarity: 0.2% w/v NaOH means 0.2 g in 100 mL. Molar mass of NaOH = 40 g/mol. Molarity M = (0.2 × 1000)/(100 × 40) = 0.05 mol/dm^3. Molar conductivity Λ_m = κ/M = (1.149 × 10^(-1))/(0.05) = 2.298 S dm^2 mol^(-1) = 229.8 × 10^(-1) mS dm^2 mol^(-1) = 23 × 10^2 mS dm^2 mol^(-1). Rounding to nearest integer: 23 × 10^2
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The standard cell potential (E°cell) of a fuel cell based on the oxidation of methanol in air that has been used to power television relay station is measured as 1.21 V. The standard half cell reduction potential for O2 (E°O2/H2O) is 1.229 V. Choose the correct statement: 1) Oxygen is formed at the anode 2) The standard half-cell reduction potential for the reduction of CO2 (E°CO2/CH3OH) is 19 mV 3) Reduction of methanol takes place at the cathode 4) Reactants are fed at one go to each electrode
options: Oxygen is formed at the anode
The standard half-cell reduction potential for the reduction of CO2 (E°CO2/CH3OH) is 19 mV
Reduction of methanol takes place at the cathode
Reactants are fed at one go to each electrode
questions.sol_text: In a fuel cell: Methanol (fuel) is oxidized at the anode, O2 (oxidant) is reduced at the cathode. Given E°cell = 1.21 V and E°O2/H2O = 1.229 V. Using E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode: 1.21 = 1.229 - E°anode, so E°anode = 0.019 V = 19 mV. This is the oxidation potential of methanol, which relates to the reduction potential of CO2/CH3OH couple. Statement 2 is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: 40 mL of a mixture of CH3COOH and HCl (aqueous solution) is titrated against 0.1 M NaOH solution conductometrically. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: Point 'C' indicates the complete neutralization of HCl
The concentration of HCl in the original mixture is 0.005 M
The concentration of CH3COOH in the original mixture is 0.005 M
CH3COOH is neutralized first followed by neutralization of HCl
questions.sol_text: In conductometric titration of a mixture of strong acid (HCl) and weak acid (CH3COOH) with NaOH: HCl (strong acid) is neutralized first because strong acids ionize completely and react faster. The conductance decreases initially as H+ ions (high conductivity) are replaced by Na+ ions (lower conductivity). At point B (around 2.0 mL), HCl is completely neutralized. Then CH3COOH is neutralized from point B to point C (5.0 mL). After point C, excess NaOH causes conductance to increase again. Therefore, statement 1 is correct: Point C indicates complete neutralization of the acid mixture (HCl neutralized at B, CH3COOH at C). Using V1=2.0 mL for HCl and total V=5.0 mL: moles of HCl = 0.1 × 0.002 = 0.0002 mol, concentration = 0.0002/0.04 = 0.005 M. For CH3COOH: moles = 0.1 × (0.005-0.002) = 0.0003 mol, concentration = 0.0003/0.04 = 0.0075 M. Statement 2 is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Correct order of limiting molar conductivity for cations in water at 298 K is:
questions.sol_text: Limiting molar conductivity depends on ion mobility in water. H+ has the highest conductivity due to its small size and special mechanism (Grotthuss mechanism). Among alkali metals, conductivity follows the order of decreasing ionic radius and hydration: Na+ > K+ (K+ is larger). For divalent cations, smaller size leads to higher hydration and lower mobility. Order: Mg2+ is highly hydrated (small), Ca2+ less hydrated. Thus: H+ > Na+ > K+ > Ca2+ > Mg2+

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For a closed circuit Daniell cell, which of the following plots is the accurate one at a given temperature?
options: E°_cell vs time showing a vertical line
E°_cell vs time showing a horizontal line that drops to a lower horizontal line
E°_cell vs time showing a decreasing linear trend
E°_cell vs time showing an increasing linear trend
questions.sol_text:
E°_cell remain constant with time.

For a closed circuit Daniell cell (galvanic cell) at a given temperature, the standard cell potential E°_cell is a thermodynamic property that depends only on the nature of the electrodes and electrolytes, and the temperature. It does NOT depend on time.

Therefore, E°_cell remains constant with time at a fixed temperature.

Analyzing the plots:
(1) Shows E°_cell as a vertical line - not realistic representation
(2) Shows E°_cell as constant (horizontal line) at a given temperature, which may show a step change if temperature changes - this is the correct representation
(3) Shows E°_cell decreasing with time - incorrect, as E°_cell does not change with time at constant temperature
(4) Shows E°_cell increasing with time - incorrect, as E°_cell does not change with time at constant temperature

The correct answer is plot (2), which shows E°_cell remaining constant (horizontal line) with time at a given temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In the given electrochemical cell, Ag(s)|AgCl(s)|FeCl2(aq), FeCl3(aq)|Pt(s) at 298 K, the cell potential (E_cell) will increase when:
questions.sol_text:
Cl^-_aq + Ag_(s) + Fe^3+_aq → Fe^2+_aq + AgCl_(s)

E_cell = E^0_cell - (0.059/1) log([Fe^2+]/([Cl^-][Fe^3+]))

From the Nernst equation, E_cell increases when the logarithmic term becomes more negative (i.e., when the argument of the logarithm decreases).

The argument [Fe^2+]/([Cl^-][Fe^3+]) decreases when:
- [Fe^2+] decreases (option C is correct)
- [Fe^3+] increases (option D is correct)
- [Cl^-] increases (option E is correct)

Therefore, E_cell increases for options C, D, and E.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider the following electrochemical cell: Pt|O2(g)(bar)|HCl(aq)||M^(2+)(aq,1.0M)|M(s). The pH above which, oxygen gas would start to evolve at anode is ____ (nearest integer). Given: E°_(M^(2+)/M) = 0.994 V, E°_(O2/H2O) = 1.23 V, and (RT/F)(2.303) = 0.059 V at the given condition.
questions.sol_text:
For spontaneity E_cell > 0

At limiting condition:
E_Oxi(anode) = -E_Red(cathode)

Oxidation at anode: H2O → 2H^+ + (1/2)O2 + 2e^-

Reduction at cathode: M^(2+) + 2e^- → M, E°_Red = -0.994 V

For oxygen oxidation:
E = E° - (0.059/2) log([H^+]^2 × p_(O2)^(1/2)/1)

At limiting condition:
-E_Oxi = E_Red
-E_O2/H2O = -(-0.994)
-(1.23 - (0.059/2) log([H^+]^2 × p_(O2)^(1/2))) = -0.994

-1.23 + 0.0295 log([H^+]^2 × p_(O2)^(1/2)) = -0.994

0.0295 log([H^+]^2 × p_(O2)^(1/2)) = 1.23 - 0.994 = 0.236

log([H^+]^2 × p_(O2)^(1/2)) = 0.236/0.0295 = 8

Assuming p_(O2) = 1 bar:
log([H^+]^2) = 8
2 log[H^+] = 8
log[H^+] = 4
[H^+] = 10^(-4) M

pH = 4
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider the following electrochemical cell at 298 K: Pt|HSnO2^-(aq)|Sn(OH)6^(2-)(aq)|Bi2O3(s)|Bi(s). If the reaction quotient at a given time is 10^6, then the cell EMF (E_cell) is ____ ×10^(-1) V (Nearest integer). Given the standard half-cell reduction potential as E°_(Bi2O3/Bi,OH^-) = -0.44 V and E°_(Sn(OH)6^(2-)/HSnO2^-,OH^-) = -0.90 V
questions.sol_text:
E°_cell = -0.44 - (-0.90) = +0.46 V

Applying Nernst equation:
E_cell = E°_cell - (0.06/n)log(Q)

E_cell = 0.46 - (0.06/6)log(10^6)

E_cell = 0.46 - (0.06/6) × 6

E_cell = 0.46 - 0.06

E_cell = 0.40 V

E_cell = 4 × 10^(-1) V

x = 4
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.text:
Molar conductivity of a weak acid HQ of concentration 0.18 M was found to be 1/30 of the molar conductivity of another weak acid HZ with concentration 0.02 of M. If lambda_Q^0 happened to be equal with lambda_Z^0, then the difference of the pK_a values of the two weak acids (pK_a(HQ) - pK_a(HZ)) is ____ (Nearest integer).

alpha_1 = lambda_m(HQ) / lambda_m^infinity(HQ)

K_a(HZ) = C_2 alpha_2^2

alpha_2 = lambda_m(HZ) / lambda_m^infinity(HZ)

K_a(HQ) / K_a(HZ) = (C_1 / C_2) * (alpha_1 / alpha_2)^2 = 0.18 / 0.02 * [lambda_m(HQ) / lambda_m(HZ)]^2

Given: lambda_m(HQ) = (1/30) * lambda_m(HZ)

K_a(HQ) / K_a(HZ) = 9 * (1/30)^2 = 9 * (1/900) = 1/100

pK_a(HQ) - pK_a(HZ) = 2

questions.text:
A volume of x mL of 5M NaHCO3 solution was mixed with 10 mL of 2M H2CO3 solution to make an electrolytic buffer. If the same buffer was used in the following electrochemical cell to record a cell potential of 235.3 mV, then the value of x = ____ mL (nearest integer).

Sn(s)|Sn(OH)2^2-(0.5M)|HSnO2^-(0.05M)|OH^-|BiO3^-|Bi(s)

Consider up to one place of decimal for intermediate calculations

Given: E°[Sn(OH)2^2-]/HSnO2^- = -0.9 V
E°Bi2O3/Bi = -0.44 V
pKa(H2CO3) = 6.11
2.303RT/F = 0.059 V
Anti log(1.29) = 19.5
questions.sol_text:
We have considered E°[Sn(OH)2^2-]/HSnO2^- = -0.9 V

Pt|HSnO2^-(aq),[Sn(OH)2^2-](aq),OH^-(aq)|BiO3^-(s)|Bi(s)|
0.5M          0.05M

E°cell = +0.9 - 0.44 = 0.46 V

Oxidation Half:
HSnO2^- + H2O + 3OH^- → [Sn(OH)2^2-]^+ + 2e^-

Reduction Half:
BiO3^- + 3H2O + 6e^- → 2Bi + 6OH^-

3HSnO2^-(aq) + BiO3^-(s) + 6H2O + 3OH^-(aq) → 3[Sn(OH)2^2-](aq) + 2Bi(s)

Ecell = E°cell - (0.059/6)log[(0.5)^3/((0.05)^3 × [OH^-]^3)]

0.2353 = 0.46 - (0.059/6) × 3log[10/[OH^-]]

log[10/[OH^-]] = (2 × 0.2247)/0.059 = 7.6

1 + pOH = 7.6
pOH = 6.6
pH = 14 - 6.6 = 7.4

Using Henderson-Hasselbalch equation:
pH = pKa + log([HCO3^-]/[H2CO3])

7.4 = 6.11 + log(5x/20)

1.29 = log(5x/4)

5x/4 = 19.5

x = 78
